text:
maya: Hey all — kicking off bring-up notes for the 13B-4bit quant + speculative decoding with an early-exit affinity heuristic. Posting quick summary + config + checklist.

chetan: nice — what's the perf/quality tradeoff so far?

maya: short answer: ~1.6x end-to-end tokens/sec in our microbench (median latency down), quality drop mostly on long, open-ended generation (coherence at 800+ tokens). Exact numbers below.

olivia: can you paste the exact inference config?

maya: sure — this is what I used for the canary runs:

```yaml
model: redwood/13b-q4
kernel: cuda-llama-opt
speculative: true
speculative_config:
  early_exit_affinity: true    # affinity based on softmax entropy + token-level logit gap
  prefills: 4                # speculative batch size for prefix tokens
  fallback_threshold: 0.65   # confidence threshold to accept early exit
  max_early_tokens: 256
  probe_interval: 8
  safety_mode: true           # disable early-exit for safety/TOU prompts
quantization: q4f32
batching: continuous
max_length: 2048
```

samir: what is "affinity" in practice? threshold on entropy?

maya: affinity = normalized (logit_gap / entropy) over last k tokens (k=16). High affinity => stable distribution => allow early-exit if cumulative prob mass > fallback_threshold. We tuned to avoid hallucination spikes.

liam: which eval sets you ran?

maya: two pass:
- offline holdout: longform QA (team-curated, 1.2k prompts, avg ground truth length 820 tokens)
- generation stability set: 400 adversarial instruction prompts (focus on self-consistency)
- short-answer extraction: 5k QA pairs (to check factual precision)
- human A/B on 200 sampled long responses (blind)

chetan: numbers?

maya: aggregated: 
- throughput (tokens/sec): baseline FP16 = 320 tps, q4 speculative (with affinity) = 512 tps (~1.6x)
- median latency per request (avg 600 tokens): baseline = 760ms, q4-spec = 470ms
- ROUGE-L on longform: baseline = 0.62, q4-spec = 0.58 (-4 pts)
- answer accuracy (short QA): baseline = 0.84, q4-spec = 0.83 (-1 pt)
- human pref (200 pairs): prefer baseline 58%, q4-spec 42% (mostly due to occasional early truncation on edge cases)

olivia: where is quality regression concentrated? specific failure modes?

maya: main patterns:
- topic drift after 900 tokens (early exits sometimes cut subtle planning tokens)
- occasional premature stop when affinity spikes on repetitive tokens (safety-mode fixes many)
- slight reduction in named-entity continuity (quantization noise)

liam: did you try turning down fallback_threshold to reduce regressions?

maya: yes — grid: {0.55, 0.60, 0.65, 0.7}. Lower threshold improves quality but reduces speed (0.55 => 1.35x, 0.65 => 1.6x). We landed on 0.65 for canary; opens for A/B.

samir: what's rollout plan? can ops do a canary in prod?

maya: propose staged canary: 1) internal infra-only shadow for 24h (no user traffic), 2) 5% canary on non-critical routes (chatbot helper) for 48h, 3) expand to 20% if metrics stable for 6h. Fallback policy: automatic reroute to FP16 13B if (a) RL-quality drop > 3% over 1h, or (b) error rate > 0.5%.

ops-bot: deploy request queued — canary env: canary-13b-q4. Tag: bringup/early-affinity-1778.

chetan: eval methodology question: are you scoring after applying reranking or any postprocessing?

maya: no rerank in these benchmarks. We keep raw generations. For production we plan a lightweight rerank for hallucination penalties (separate PR). We also ran with and without KV-cache warmup — caching improves stability a touch.

olivia: metrics to watch in console?

maya: add these dashboards: 
- per-route avg token latency (1m/1h)
- human-pref proxy: perplexity surge on the last 200 tokens
- early-exit rate (%) by route
- fallback rate and latencies on fallback
- regression alert: 1h rolling ROUGE-L delta

liam: any weird infra observations?

maya: 2 oddities: 1) small memory jitter when speculative prefill=8 on certain A100 drivers -> OOMs in 1/500 runs. We set prefill=4 for canary. 2) quant kernels slightly slower for batch sizes < 2 because vectorized kernels assume larger warp loads. Ops aware.

samir: safety checks?

maya: we flagged safety waivers: disable early-exit for prompts matching safety regexes, and add synthetic safety set to A/B to ensure no increase in toxic output. Also short-circuit early-exit on system messages.

chetan: what's our hypothesis for where affinity helps most?

maya: hypothesis: speculative early-exit is best for 'procedural' or 'deterministic' continuations (code, step lists). It hurts more on open creative tasks that rely on long-range planning. So route-level policy makes sense.

liam: action items?

maya: short list: 
- ops: stand up 5% canary route & attach dashboards (liam)
- eval: run 10k human-proxy runs with adjusted thresholds (chel) -> olivia
- infra: pin prefill=4 and driver version (samir)
- product: pick 2 non-critical routes for canary (chat-snippet + docs-summary)

olivia: noted. i'll scope the human A/B script and add sampling strat for long responses.

chetan: one more — can we capture the model logits and affinity stream for a sample of canary requests? useful for debugging.

maya: yes, store logits (topk=16) for 1% of canary traffic with redaction. adding as flag: `capture_affinity_trace=true`.

liam: +1, also add a lightweight SHA of model + quant config to every trace.

maya: thanks — i'll open the PR for canary config and a short eval tracker doc. Will post links here when ready. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: canary deployment started: canary-13b-q4 on 3 nodes. Monitor at https://internal.console/redwood/canaries/bringup-1778234567

maya: posting initial PRs: 
- infra: github.com/redwood/inference/pull/4217 (canary config)
- eval: github.com/redwood/evals/pull/98 (holdout datasets + runner)

chetan: great. keep notes here for retrospective.

maya: will do. next update after 24h shadow and first 5% canary results.

end of thread.
